traits.height_max_m.note: Silvics vol. 1 (1990), Grand Fir chapter (Foiles, Graham and Olson): mature trees on optimum coastal Washington sites reach 43 to 61 m, occasionally 76 m; normally 35 to 46 m in northern Idaho, 30 to 40 m on eastern Oregon pumice, 15 to 21 m on exposed Inland Empire ridges; an Olympic Peninsula tree measured 70.4 m.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Fir, grand, green: modulus of elasticity 8,600 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.35).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Fir, grand, green: modulus of rupture 40,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Fir, grand: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 91% and sapwood 136% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Abies grandis (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.37 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 6 records in 6 sources); trunks 0.36, branches 0.45. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: FEIS's grand fir review: needles kept seven years on average; Abrams's genus gives usually 8 to 10.

traits.foliage_ranks.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 66): needles 35 to 50 mm, flat and flexible, glossy above and silvery beneath, in two ranks making flat sprays. His seed cone of 12 to 18 cm reads clearly but is long for the species, so no cone length is stated until a second source checks it.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 66): needles 35 to 50 mm, flat and flexible, glossy above and silvery beneath, in two ranks making flat sprays. His seed cone of 12 to 18 cm reads clearly but is long for the species, so no cone length is stated until a second source checks it.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Howard and Aleksoff 2000, read): cone and seed production begins at 20 to 50 years of age. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Abies, table 3, read) gives 20 as the minimum age for commercial seed bearing in northern Idaho. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 20 years set by hand.

generator.params.apical.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): fitted with the family's ramifying crown (side_order 2, twig_years 10) so the drawn crown's widths at each tenth of height match the photographed open-grown trees': young (3 trees) .67 .71 .69 .63 .55 .42 .36 .25 .16 .09; old (1) .50 .64 .67 .65 .61 .50 .57 .58 .45 .28; drawn 60 years .65 .64 .59 .56 .51 .44 .38 .31 .18 .07; 300 years .47 .54 .50 .50 .43 .40 .36 .31 .28 .11. apical sets the young crown's width.

generator.params.branch_reach.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): fitted with the family's ramifying crown (side_order 2, twig_years 10) so the drawn crown's widths at each tenth of height match the photographed open-grown trees': young (3 trees) .67 .71 .69 .63 .55 .42 .36 .25 .16 .09; old (1) .50 .64 .67 .65 .61 .50 .57 .58 .45 .28; drawn 60 years .65 .64 .59 .56 .51 .44 .38 .31 .18 .07; 300 years .47 .54 .50 .50 .43 .40 .36 .31 .28 .11. branch_reach, the wood at which a limb's yearly shoot is halved, sets how far old limbs spread.

generator.params.bole.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): the share of an old tree's height cleared of limbs, cleared in step with height so saplings keep limbs to the ground: open-grown trees photographed keep limbs nearly to the ground at every stage (crown base .03 young, .05 old).

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall fir with a narrow, domed crown, level branches and flat sprays of long, glossy needles in two ranks. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): 6 to 11 cm stand upright on the top branches and shed their scales on the tree; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `cone_pitch`, `cone_years`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 33 m tall and 50 cm across at breast height at 60 years in a closed stand. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy dark green needles; smooth grey bark with resin blisters, furrowed with age. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): flat needles 2 to 5 cm long and about 2 mm wide, so a needle 0.065 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth and grey with resin blisters when young, then furrowed into flat grey-brown ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
